title: CBC Theatre 10:30
paragraphs: A CBC radio-drama anthology represented here by a small collection of standalone plays. Because surviving catalog information is uneven, this description avoids assigning unsupported dates or a single recurring premise.

CBC dramatic anthology preserved in thirteen frozen recordings. Chronology is disputed: the preservation catalog treats the collection as 1961-era and one file is dated 1961-08-28, while other references place Theatre 10:30 in 1968-71. Most exact dates are not safely recoverable.
GRH documents the program through CBC Theatre 10:30 chronology-disputed run (1961 to 1971) on [[org|org.vp.4ad028d3bc03e0f3|CBC Radio]].
Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Anthony Lee Flanders (writer on 2 recordings), Alan King (writer on 1 recording), and Betty Lambert (writer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Canadian radio drama, classic literary adaptation, horror and supernatural fiction, science fiction and speculative fiction, wilderness and isolation, and psychological horror and obsession.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including CBC dramatic anthology tradition, Theatre 10:30 chronology dispute, Mid-century radio adaptation of classic horror and speculative literature, and Klondike gold-rush historical setting.

A CBC radio-drama anthology represented here by a small collection of standalone plays. Because surviving catalog information is uneven, this description avoids assigning unsupported dates or a single recurring premise.

CBC dramatic anthology preserved in thirteen frozen recordings. Chronology is disputed: the preservation catalog treats the collection as 1961-era and one file is dated 1961-08-28, while other references place Theatre 10:30 in 1968-71. Most exact dates are not safely recoverable.

GRH documents the program through CBC Theatre 10:30 chronology-disputed run (1961 to 1971) on CBC Radio.

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are Anthony Lee Flanders (writer on 2 recordings), Alan King (writer on 1 recording), and Betty Lambert (writer on 1 recording).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include Canadian radio drama, classic literary adaptation, horror and supernatural fiction, science fiction and speculative fiction, wilderness and isolation, and psychological horror and obsession.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including CBC dramatic anthology tradition, Theatre 10:30 chronology dispute, Mid-century radio adaptation of classic horror and speculative literature, and Klondike gold-rush historical setting.
